original_finding.first_contract: ArchitecturalPlanPoint accepts all finite f32 coordinates. PlanPolygon promises finite, nondegenerate counterclockwise convex vertices and calculates its area using f64 differences after widening. PlanHull uses the same f64 difference-and-cross operation to distinguish segment and area.
original_finding.symbolic_source_reasoning: Let t=2^-100, exactly representable as a positive finite f32, and take A=(t,0), B=(2,2), C=(1,1). The exact real determinant (B−A)×(C−A) is t > 0, so A,B,C form a nondegenerate counterclockwise triangle. In binary64 subtraction, 2−t rounds to 2 and 1−t rounds to 1; the calculated translated vectors become (2,2) and (1,1), whose computed cross and signed area are zero. Source control flow therefore returns DegeneratePolygon before later checks. In the monotone-hull sorting order A,C,B, both forward and reverse crosses round to zero, so its source algorithm discards C and classifies the set as a Segment. This is symbolic IEEE-754 arithmetic, not a product invocation, generated fixture, probe or test.
original_finding.consumers: CollisionCuboid::ground_contact projects checked 3D corners/intersections to ArchitecturalPlanPoint and classifies via PlanHull. BuildingCollision::ground_floor_footprint returns Some only for an Area; compiled city seating and envelope paths map None to MissingBearing. These references establish possible downstream roles, not that any supported cuboid, building, or real plan can produce the symbolic point set.
